cohort: 1080 postpartum women who were normotensive during pregnancy and the antepartum period, and delivered at the B.P. Koirala Institute of Health Sciences between March 2020-May 2020
finding: The incidence of de novo postpartum hypertension (dPPHTN) was 4.9%, and cesarean delivery was significantly associated with dPPHTN, while parity, family history of hypertension, and multiple gestations were not.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was found to have a statistically significant association with dPPHTN.
followup_time: Variable, up to 14 days postpartum, with attempts made to contact patients via telephone
